title: Pulse-pressure–pulse product adds no demonstrated albuminuria prediction beyond standard risk factors across two NHANES surveys
abstract: In a frozen survey-weighted logistic model trained on 4,789 NHANES 2009–2010 adults and tested on 4,480 independently sampled 2015–2016 adults, adding pulse pressure times resting pulse changed Brier score from 0.07595942 to 0.07600691: difference +0.00004749, approximate target-PSU bootstrap 95% interval -0.00001606 to +0.00011432. AUC changed by -0.00005003. Main-effect squares, alternative blood-pressure bases, penalty changes and macroalbuminuria exclusion did not reveal a predictive gain. This negative result concerns incremental prediction of a single spot-urine outcome, not absence of physiological pulsatile injury or equivalence of all learning procedures.
